title: Administration
intro: Configure the platform, manage accounts, and review usage.

settings.registerDesc: Let visitors create their own account from the sign-up page.
settings.newAccountQuotaHelp: Seeded from the <env></env> environment variable. Per-account limits are edited in the Users tab.
settings.registerAdminNote: This only governs strangers signing themselves up. You can always create an account from the Users tab, whatever this is set to.
settings.keyDesc: When a key is set, a self-service sign-up has to quote it as well. Leave it empty and anyone may sign up while the switch above is on.
settings.keyPlaceholder: No key: anyone may sign up
settings.keyKeepPlaceholder: Leave empty to keep the current key
settings.keyRemovePending: The key will be removed when you save.
settings.keyInactive: A key only applies while self-service sign-up is on. It never opens a closed sign-up: to let one person in, create their account in the Users tab.
settings.keyUndecryptable: The stored key cannot be read any more (the encryption key changed). Type a new one to replace it.
settings.keyUnreadable: The stored key could not be read.

users.searchPlaceholder: Search by name, email or tag…
users.createFirst: Create the first account to get started.
users.showing: Showing {filtered} of {total, plural, one {# user} other {# users}}.
users.createDesc: Accounts created here work whether or not self-service sign-up is open.
users.name: Name
users.editDesc: Identity, address, sign-in, storage and permissions for {email}.
users.usernameHelp: Can be typed instead of the email address when signing in. Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores. Leave empty to remove it.
users.emailHelp: Used to sign in and to receive password resets. Changing it takes effect at once.
users.emailHelpUnverified: This address has never been confirmed. Setting it here marks it as verified, so the account can sign in.
users.newPasswordPlaceholder: Leave empty to keep the current one
users.newPasswordHelp: The current password cannot be shown: only a hash of it is stored. Setting a new one signs the account out everywhere.
users.newPasswordHelpNone: This account has no password login yet (imported without one). Setting a password here creates it.
users.selfLockoutHint: This is the account you are signed in with, so its role and status are locked. An administrator cannot demote or block themselves.
users.publicProfileDesc: Publish this account's files as a browsable gallery at /u/{tag}.
users.skipTagDesc: New uploads get links like host/name.png instead of host/tag/name.png. The root namespace is shared with every top-level route, so codes can collide with app pages. Links already shared keep working.
users.confirmSensitiveTitle: You are about to change how {name} signs in.
users.confirmEmail: Email: {from} becomes {to}. The old address stops working immediately.
users.confirmPassword: A new password is set and every session of this account is signed out.
users.confirmPasswordSelf: A new password is set and every session is signed out - including this one, so you will have to sign in again.
users.noteEmail: Signs in with {email} from now on.
users.notePassword: All sessions of this account were signed out.

name.empty: A display name cannot be empty.

username.charset: A login name is 2 to 32 characters: letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, starting with a letter or digit.
username.taken: Another account already uses that login name.

email.invalid: That does not look like an email address.
email.taken: Another account already uses that email address.

password.too-short: A password needs at least 8 characters.
password.too-long: A password can be at most 128 characters.

quota.invalid: Enter a size such as 20G, 512M or 1T.

role.self: You cannot change your own role. Ask another administrator.

banned.self: You cannot block the account you are signed in with.

users.tagHelp: First segment of every public link. The previous tag keeps resolving forever, so links already shared never break.

tagIssue.too-short: A tag needs at least 2 characters.
tagIssue.too-long: A tag can be at most 32 characters.
tagIssue.charset: Use letters, digits, dashes and underscores only, starting with a letter or digit.
tagIssue.reserved: That tag is reserved by the application.
tagIssue.taken: Another account already uses that tag.
tagIssue.retired: Another account used that tag before - it can never be reassigned.
tagIssue.error: Something went wrong. Please try again.

users.quotaHelp: Currently using {used}. Uploads past the limit are rejected with 507.
users.quotaInvalidDesc: Enter a size such as 20G, 512M or 1T.
users.rootLinksDesc: Allow this account to create short links without its tag prefix. The root namespace is shared with every top-level route.
users.removeConfirm: {email} will be signed out and removed, along with their folders, short links and API tokens. This cannot be undone.
users.dispDeleteDesc: Erase every upload and free the disk space.
users.dispKeepDesc: Keep the bytes, without an owner.
users.dispDeleteWarning: The files and their bytes are destroyed for good - links already shared will stop working and nothing can bring them back.
users.dispKeepWarning: The files stay on disk but lose their public links (the address starts with the owner's tag). They move to Orphaned files, where you can review or delete them later.
users.removedPurged: {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} deleted, {size} freed.
users.removedKept: {count, plural, one {# file is} other {# files are}} now orphaned.
users.removeFailedTitle: Some files could not be deleted
users.removeFailedDesc: Storage refused {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}. They are listed under Orphaned files - try again from there.

removeReason.self: You cannot delete the account you are signed in with.
removeReason.forbidden: The account could not be removed. Try again.
removeReason.files-removed: The files were deleted, but the account itself could not be removed. Try again.

users.passwordRequired: A password is required for this option.
users.createModeQuestion: How does this person get in the first time?
users.modeInviteDesc: They choose their own password from a mailed link. Nothing to pass on by hand, and no password exists in the meantime.
users.modeInviteUnavailable: Needs outgoing mail. Set it up in the Mail tab.
users.modePasswordDesc: You pick it and pass it on yourself.
users.modePasswordHint: You have to give this password to the user yourself. The address counts as confirmed, so they can sign in straight away.

createReason.invalid-email: That does not look like an email address.
createReason.weak-password: A password needs at least 8 characters.
createReason.taken: Another account already uses that email address.
createReason.mail-unavailable: Invitations need outgoing mail. Set it up in the Mail tab, or set a password here instead.
createReason.failed: The account could not be created. Try again.

users.createdInviteFailed: The account exists, but the invitation to {email} could not be sent. Check the Mail tab, then send it again from the row menu.

mailReason.mail-unavailable: Outgoing mail is not configured. Set it up in the Mail tab.
mailReason.send-failed: The mail server refused the message. The Mail tab has a test button that reports why.

orphans.title: Files without an owner
orphans.intro: These uploads outlived the account that created them - someone was deleted with “keep the files”. They are not reachable on the web any more (a public link starts with the owner's tag), but their bytes still occupy the disk.
orphans.showingCapped: Showing the {shown} oldest of {total}. Delete some, or use “Delete all”.
orphans.emptyHint: Every file on this install belongs to an account.
orphans.deleteGone: It was already deleted, or it now belongs to an account again.
orphans.purgeDesc: This removes {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} and frees {size}.
orphans.purgeWarning: The bytes are erased from storage, not moved to the trash. There is no way back.
orphans.purgeCta: Delete {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}
orphans.purgeEmpty: There is nothing left to delete.
orphans.purgeMismatch: The number didn't match. It changes whenever the list does - reopen the dialog and use the current count.
orphans.purgedDesc: {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} removed, {size} freed.
orphans.purgeFailedDesc: Storage refused {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}. They are still listed - try again in a moment.

maintenance.recalcDesc: Rebuilds every account's used-space counter from the files that actually exist. The counter is updated as files come and go, so it only drifts after something happens outside the app - a hand-written database fix, an interrupted import, or an account deleted with its files kept. Trashed files count: they still occupy the disk.
maintenance.recalcClean: All {accounts, plural, one {# account was} other {# accounts were}} already correct.
maintenance.recalcCorrected: Corrected {corrected} of {accounts, plural, one {# account} other {# accounts}}.
maintenance.scanTitle: Scan for files with no database row
maintenance.scanDesc: Walks the storage directory and reports objects that no upload points at - the mirror image of an orphaned row. They are usually left by an interrupted upload or a row deleted by hand. Files touched in the last hour are skipped: an upload being finalised right now looks exactly like one of these.
maintenance.scanClean: All {scanned, plural, one {# object} other {# objects}} on disk are accounted for.
maintenance.scanFound: {count, plural, one {# object} other {# objects}} with no database row, {size}.
maintenance.scanUnsupported: This install stores files in an object store (S3). Listing a bucket is a paid, paginated API, so the scan only runs against local storage.
maintenance.scanScanned: {count, plural, one {# object scanned} other {# objects scanned}}
maintenance.scanSkipped: {count, plural, one {# too recent} other {# too recent}}
maintenance.scanTruncated: The scan hit its file limit and stopped early - the numbers below are a lower bound.
maintenance.scanReportOnly: Report only. Nothing is deleted here: removing an object that an upload is still finalising would destroy a file that is arriving right now. Verify a path before removing it by hand.

disk.title: Server disk
disk.descLocal: Space on the filesystem that stores the uploads. Everything else on this machine shares it.
disk.descObject: Files live in an object store ({driver}), which has no server disk to fill. These are the totals the database accounts for.
disk.descUnmeasured: The filesystem could not be measured on this host, so only the totals the database accounts for are shown.
disk.criticalNote: Free space is critical. A full disk takes down everything else running on this machine, not just uploads.
disk.reserveNote: Uploads are refused once less than {size} is free.
disk.insightsDesc: Counted in the database over the size recorded for every file. Thumbnails and cached conversions sit on the same storage but are not rows here, so they are not in these totals.
disk.insightsDescObject: Counted in the database over the size recorded for every file. What {driver} actually holds can only be more: thumbnails, cached conversions and the leftovers of an interrupted upload are objects no row here accounts for, and nothing short of listing the bucket can count them.
disk.kindsDesc: Live files, grouped by what each file actually is rather than by the name it was given.
disk.accountsDesc: Everything an account holds, trash included. The tail is folded into one row rather than dropped, so the column still adds up.
disk.accountsRest: {count, plural, one {# other account} other {# other accounts}}
disk.biggestDesc: Live files, largest first. These free the most space per decision.
disk.coldTotal: in {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}
disk.coldEmpty: Everything stored has been fetched within the last {days} days.
disk.coldNote: Access has been counted only since a file's row was created here. Files that predate the counter, or were imported, carry no history at all, so a file with no recorded access is not proof that nobody ever opened it.
disk.trashDesc: Soft-deleted files. Their bytes stay on the storage until the sweeper purges them after {days} days.
disk.trashOldestHint: Time since it was moved to the trash
disk.trashOverdue: {size} in {count, plural, one {# file is} other {# files are}} past the {days} day window and still stored. The purge job is not running.

mail.title: Outgoing mail (SMTP)
mail.intro: Password resets, address confirmations and invitations all travel through this server. Without it those features are simply off.
mail.fromEnv: This configuration comes from the environment (SMTP_HOST and friends). The fields stay read-only until you take it over here.
mail.overridesEnv: These settings override the SMTP_HOST in the environment.
mail.userPlaceholder: Leave empty for a server without authentication
mail.passwordKeep: Leave empty to keep the stored password
mail.passwordSet: A password is stored. It is encrypted at rest and never sent back to the browser, so this field is always empty.
mail.passwordUnset: No password is stored. Leave it that way for a server that does not ask for one.
mail.passwordUnreadable: The stored password can no longer be decrypted, which usually means AUTH_SECRET changed. Mail stays off until you type it again.
mail.savedDesc: Send a test message to confirm the server accepts them.

invalid.invalid-host: That server name does not look usable.
invalid.invalid-from: The sender address is not a valid email address.
invalid.invalid-port: A port is a number between 1 and 65535.
invalid.password-required: This server needs a password for that user name. Type one in before saving, or clear the user name.

mail.revertedDesc: The values saved here were removed.
mail.verificationOn: New accounts now have to confirm their address.
mail.verificationOff: New accounts can sign in without confirming their address.
mail.testDesc: A real message, not just a connection check: the failure that trips most installs is the server refusing the sender address, and that only shows up once a message is on the wire.
mail.testUnavailable: Fill in the server details above first.
mail.testFailedTitle: The test could not be run

testError.not-configured: Mail is not configured, so nothing was sent.
testError.rate-limited: Too many tests in a row. Try again in a few minutes.
testError.auth: The server rejected the username or password.
testError.connection: The server could not be reached on that address and port.
testError.tls: The encrypted connection failed. Try a different encryption setting.
testError.recipient: The server refused the sender or the recipient address.

mail.verificationLabel: New accounts must confirm their email address
mail.verificationDesc: A confirmation link is mailed on sign-up and the account cannot sign in until it is used. Existing accounts are unaffected, and you can always confirm an address by hand from the Users tab.
mail.verificationNeedsMail: Needs a working mail server: with none, a confirmation nobody can receive would lock every new account out.

files.banner: You are viewing {name}'s files as an administrator, signed in as yourself. This visit and anything you change here is recorded in the audit log. Folders belong to the owner, so moving files is not offered.
files.emptyHint: Files uploaded by this account appear here.

release.title: {app} release
release.desc: The download button on the Integrations page points at whatever is set here.
release.none: Nothing published yet - the download button on the Integrations page stays disabled.
release.hint: Upload the installer like any other file, then paste its link here. It must be published and must NOT be password-protected - if your account stamps a default password on new uploads, clear it on this one first, otherwise the download would ask every visitor for a password.

errors.no-version: Give both a version and a link.
errors.not-found: No file with that link - check it, and that the file has not been deleted.
errors.not-public: That file is unpublished or password-protected, so nobody could download it. Publish it and clear its password, then try again.
errors.bad-version: The version must look like 0.7 or 0.7.0 or 0.7.0.1 - digits and dots only. Anything else cannot be read by an installed client, which would then report a failed check forever.
errors.version-mismatch: You typed {typed}, but the file is called {filename}, which says {fileVersion}. Publishing a version the binary does not carry makes every copy install the update and then be offered it again, at every launch. Fix the version, or press Publish anyway.
